title: finding(mobile): `useSpecGesture`'s fallback payload writes `type` BEFORE spreading the recognizer context, so the recognizer's own name overwrites the declared spec gesture — measured on `drag`, latent at two more sites
body:
Found during the in-seat review of PR objectui#9689 (card objectui#7974). The lane measured one instance and named one arm; the census below is the reviewing seat's, and it is three.

## What

`packages/mobile/src/useSpecGesture.ts` builds each gesture's fallback payload by spreading the recognizer's runtime context next to a declared `type`. Where `type` is written **before** the spread, the recognizer's own `type` — which travels inside `ctx` — overwrites it.

Measured on PR objectui#9689's head, every `fallback({ … })` call in the file:

| line | arm | spelling | `type` survives? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:117` | `swipe` | `{ ...ctx, type: 'swipe' }` | ✅ — **spread first, `type` last** |
| `:124` | `long_press` | `{ type: 'long_press' }` | ✅ — no `ctx` spread |
| `:128` | `pinch` | `{ type: 'pinch', ...ctx }` | ⛔ **overwritten** |
| `:132` | `double_tap` | `{ type: 'double_tap' }` | ✅ — no `ctx` spread |
| `:137` | `pan` / `drag` | `{ type: declared, ...ctx }` | ⛔ **overwritten** |
| `:141` | `rotate` | `{ type: 'rotate', ...ctx }` | ⛔ **overwritten** |

**Three sites carry the shape, not one.** `:117` is the one PR objectui#9689 corrected, because the ruling it executed made the recognizer say `pan` for a swipe and the wrong answer became visible.

## The measured instance

The lane ran a throwaway probe with `config: { type: 'drag', enabled: true }`, asserted the fallback payload's `type`, and got:

```
AssertionError: the DECLARED spec gesture: expected 'pan' to be 'drag'
```

The probe was removed and `git status` proved clean afterwards. ⇒ `ctx` really does carry a `type` key at runtime — which is the load-bearing fact for all three rows above, not just for that one.

## ⭐ Why the other two rows are worth filing even though they are quiet today

`pinch` and `rotate` declare the same name the recognizer uses, so the overwrite replaces a value with itself and nothing is observably wrong. **That is a coincidence of two vocabularies agreeing, not a property of the code.** `pan` / `drag` is the row where they disagree, and it is wrong there today.

⇒ These two are a **latent** instance of a defect that is already live one row up: any rename on either side — the retired `ui/touch` spec vocabulary or the `useGesture` recognizer vocabulary — turns them into the `drag` case, silently, with no gate between the two spellings. The file itself documents that the two sides ARE different vocabularies (*"Note the two sides are different vocabularies, which is why this map exists at all"*), which is exactly the condition under which relying on them agreeing is unsafe.

## Cost

A consumer's `onGesture` fallback receives the **recognizer's** name where the API's own docblock says it reports the declared spec gesture. `drag` is reported as `pan` today. Nothing refuses it and nothing logs it — the payload is well-formed and wrong.

## Shape of the remedy — ⛔ not decided here

Writing `type` last at the three sites is a two-character move per site and is what `:117` already does. ⚠️ But it is a **behaviour change to a published payload** at each one: a consumer that has been reading `'pan'` for a declared `drag` would start receiving `'drag'`. PR objectui#9689 made exactly that change for the `swipe` arm and declared it in its changeset as breaking; the same declaration is owed here, which is why this is a card rather than a follow-up commit.

⛔ objectui#7974's dispatch fenced this off explicitly — the `drag` arm is *"an unruled behaviour change to a published payload and was deliberately left alone"* — and that fence was correct.

## Adjacent, noted rather than filed separately

`SPEC_GESTURE_TYPE_MAP.swipe` is now `'swipe-left'` as a **declared placeholder**: after objectui#7974 the hook assigns `gestureType = 'pan'` for a swipe directly and never reads the map's value for that key. Measured — the only readers of that exported map are the parity test's key-set checks (`name in SPEC_GESTURE_TYPE_MAP`, and the extra-keys filter), never its values. PR objectui#9689 labels it a placeholder in a comment, which is honest; changing an exported map's value is a published-surface change that card did not rule on. Recorded here because whoever takes the rows above is in the same lines.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any consumer in this repository or downstream actually reads the fallback payload's `type` — no call-site census was taken. ⛔ Whether `pinch` and `rotate` are the whole latent population; only this one file was read. ⛔ Whether the same spread-order shape exists in the other hooks under `packages/mobile`.

Refs: objectui#7974 (the ruling whose execution surfaced this) - PR objectui#9689 (fixed the `swipe` row, fenced the rest) - objectui#2942 (the earlier repair of this hook's `config.type` handling).
